item.text: {"analysis":"The item-bias candidate failed the host’s post-training correctness check: forward adds learned item biases, while the checker requires positive scores to equal the tied-embedding dot product alone. Zero initialization preserves initial scores, but trained biases violate that requirement. Observed validation HR@10 was 0.645, 0.630, 0.615, 0.635, and 0.600 at epochs 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25. The best observed value, 0.645, tied the baseline without improving it. The run ended with status crash; no successful submission or test result was reported. Experience: additive scoring biases conflict with the frozen host’s scoring contract and showed no validation gain in this attempt.","code_summary":"Causal NextItNet with MAXLEN=128, HIDDEN_UNITS=64, NUM_BLOCKS=8, KERNEL_SIZE=3, DROPOUT_RATE=0.2, LR=0.001, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.0, and BATCH_SIZE=128. Eight independent blocks use dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8], two left-padded convolutions per block, pre-convolution LayerNorm, GELU, dropout, and learned per-channel residual scales initialized to 0.1. The backbone uses scaled tied item embeddings, padding masks after every block, final LayerNorm, and no positional embeddings. Candidate scoring uses the last valid sequence position. This attempt added zero-initialized scalar item biases to both training and candidate scores, causing the host correctness failure."}
